title: Use Hazard3
lede: Run the upstream Hazard3 CPU in a Prism SoC: fetch the tested Hazard3 version, select it in your SoC manifest, test it and build it for the board.
prerequisites: The tools from [Install tools and run a simulation](#/guides/getting-started#1-install-the-tools). You also need Git to fetch the Hazard3 source.
A SoC manifest, as in [Build a SoC and run a program on it](#/tutorials/instantiate-core).
outcome: A SoC that runs unmodified upstream Hazard3 with Prism's memory and peripherals, in simulation and on the board.

stages.title: Fetch the Hazard3 source
stages.text: Prism does not include Hazard3's source. Fetch the tested version into the place the build expects. The build then patches a copy of it for the simulator; you do nothing more unless you update Hazard3.

stages.title: Select Hazard3 in your SoC manifest
stages.text: Selecting Hazard3 is the same one-key edit as for any other core.

stages.title: Test the connection
stages.text: Hazard3 speaks AHB; Prism connects it through an adapter on each memory port. Lint the SoC and run the adapter test.

stages.title: Run firmware
stages.text: Prism compiles firmware for the instruction set Hazard3 is built with, including multiply, atomics and compressed instructions. Run a program in simulation before building for the board.

stages.title: Build it for the board
stages.text: Hazard3 needs a lower CPU clock than Base on this board. Set the clock in your system manifest, then build and program.
